comparison: Perfect agreement on methodology and HOT loci definition (C1-C4). Both evaluations find the computational analyses solid and the dataset sources, numbers, and binning approach well-justified. OpenEval emphasizes methodological transparency while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive dataset analysis.

Both support the quantitative findings about peak concentration (C5), though peer R2 groups this with broader genomic distribution claims (C6-C12) while OpenEval R2 focuses specifically on the disproportionate concentration finding with C13-C14. Both recognize this as establishing HOT loci as a major regulatory phenomenon.

Both support genomic distribution findings (C6-C8). OpenEval R3 emphasizes functional importance for gene regulation and TSS clustering, while peer R2 accepts these as part of comprehensive characterization without detailed critique. OpenEval includes C83 while peer review groups with broader chromatin features.

Both support chromatin state characterization (C9-C12). OpenEval R4 provides detailed assessment of statistical quantification and Figure 1D-E evidence, while peer R2 accepts these findings as part of the overall genomic characterization without specific methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on DAP clustering analysis (C15-C20). Both evaluations accept the hierarchical clustering methodology and functional characterization. OpenEval explicitly mentions PPI network analysis support (C86-C87) with significant p-values, while peer review focuses on the identification of invariantly associated proteins.

Both support 3D chromatin interaction findings (C22-C26, C91-C92). OpenEval R6 provides detailed statistical assessment including correlation coefficients and p-values, while peer R4 accepts the regulatory significance and chromatin interaction findings. OpenEval also addresses C88-C90 which peer R4 includes.

Both support signal strength analysis (C27-C30). OpenEval R7 notes the 1.9× effect is statistically significant but cautions about mechanistic interpretation, while peer R5 accepts the computational approaches as solid without raising concerns about the stabilizer DAP findings.

Both support the ChIP-seq signal comparison (C93-C95). OpenEval R8 notes the conclusion about DNA-binding independence is reasonable but could benefit from validation, while peer R5 accepts the correlation analyses without methodological concerns as part of solid computational work.

Both strongly support evolutionary conservation analysis (C31-C34, C76-C77). OpenEval R9 emphasizes phastCons scores and ultraconserved regions with disease gene associations, while peer R6 explicitly accepts the conservation findings as established results, noting they identify features 'enriched in these regions, their conservation in evolution.'

Perfect agreement on sequence feature analysis (C35-C38, C96-C97). Both accept the correlations and differential patterns between promoters and enhancers. OpenEval notes the 12% CpG overlap justifies conclusions about HOT enhancers, while peer review finds the GC content influence on HOT loci formation 'refreshing.'

Perfect agreement on CNN classification analysis (C39, C78, C98-C100). Both accept the model comparisons and sequence-based superiority. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation (C99) is somewhat speculative, while peer review finds the computational modeling concept 'refreshing' and accepts that HOT loci formation is embedded in DNA sequences.

Perfect agreement on expression analysis (C40-C45, C101-C102). Both support the correlations and fold-changes. OpenEval appropriately notes causal interpretation (C101) is suggested rather than proven, while peer review accepts these as part of comprehensive analyses without raising causality concerns.

Both support housekeeping gene analysis (C46-C48, C73, C103-C104). OpenEval R13 emphasizes tau score statistical support and functional distinctions, while peer R10 accepts the contrasting roles of HOT promoters (housekeeping) versus enhancers (tissue-specific) without questioning the methodology.

Both support tau score analysis (C49-C50). OpenEval R14 notes small but significant difference for enhancers and large difference for promoters with Figure 6B confirmation, while peer R10 accepts these findings as part of the functional distinction between HOT promoters and enhancers.

Both support developmental analysis (C51-C53, C105-C109) but with caveats. OpenEval R15 notes interpretation about acquisition timing is somewhat speculative and limited H1 DAPs (n=47) is a significant limitation, while peer R11 accepts the overlap analyses and distinctions between embryonic and differentiated states without raising concerns.

Both support variant analysis (C55-C56, C110). OpenEval R16 notes the paradox is acknowledged and contextualized with Vierstra citation, while peer R12 accepts variant enrichment findings as part of comprehensive analysis identifying 'variation in disease' without methodological concerns.

Both support eQTL analysis (C57-C58, C111). OpenEval R17 notes TSS-proximal bias is appropriately contextualized with GTEx citation and lack of significance for HOT enhancers is properly reported, while peer R12 accepts these QTL enrichment findings without challenge.

Both support caQTL analysis (C59-C60, C112). OpenEval R18 emphasizes strong statistical significance and appropriate citation to Currin et al. 2021, while peer R12 accepts the variant enrichment analyses as established contributions to understanding variation in disease.

Both support raQTL analysis (C61-C62, C113). OpenEval R19 notes the interpretation about methodological bias is reasonable given experimental design of van Arensbergen et al. 2019, while peer R12 accepts these findings as part of comprehensive variant enrichment analysis.

Both support GWAS analysis (C63-C64, C114-C115). OpenEval R20 notes interpretation about functional consequences is reasonable but somewhat speculative and correctly distinguishes causal versus correlative QTLs, while peer R12 accepts the GWAS enrichment findings without raising concerns about causal interpretation.

Both support GWAS trait analysis (C116-C119). OpenEval R21 notes appropriate multiple testing correction and tissue-specific validation, finding phenotypic homeostasis conclusion reasonable, while peer R12 accepts these findings as part of the comprehensive variant enrichment analysis.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN regarding condensate involvement (C65-C71, C120-C123). OpenEval R22 notes individual observations are well-supported but overall condensate conclusion is explicitly speculative with correlative rather than mechanistic evidence. Peer R13 initially requested toning down speculation but after revisions found Figure 9 'particularly compelling,' accepting evidence with uncertainty about mechanism.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN the speculative condensate model (C82, C125-C128). OpenEval R23 notes this is explicitly acknowledged as hypothesis requiring experimental validation, conceptually coherent but untested. Peer R13 shows same pattern: initial concern about speculation, acceptance after revisions with acknowledgment that authors explicitly state it as speculative hypothesis.

Both support overarching conclusions about HOT loci challenging classical models (C72, C80-C81). OpenEval R24 emphasizes cumulative evidence particularly C5 showing 51% of peaks in 5% of loci, while peer R14 finds the study 'valuable' and notes it contributes to knowledge with appropriate contextualization of the paradigm shift.

Both support tissue-specific function of HOT enhancers (C74). OpenEval R25 cites tau score analysis, GO enrichment, and tissue-specific pioneer factors as converging evidence, while peer R10 accepts the contrasting roles with HOT enhancers regulating tissue-specific processes.

OpenEval R26 supports super-enhancer relationship (C75) but notes claim is somewhat overstated - HOT loci enriched but don't constitute majority of super-enhancer sequence. Peer R2 accepts super-enhancer findings as part of chromatin feature characterization without noting this nuance.

Both support abstract summary about sequence features and expression (C79). OpenEval R27 notes this is justified by detailed analyses of sequence correlations and expression relationships, while peer R14 accepts the study's contributions as appropriately summarized.

OpenEval R28 supports comparison with prior studies (C85) showing high overlap and conservation, noting 400bp windows capture core regions of 2kb windows. Peer R1 accepts the computational analyses as solid without specifically addressing this comparison claim.

OpenEval R29 supports PPI network analysis (C86-C87) with highly significant enrichment providing functional context for DAP clusters. Peer R3 accepts the clustering analysis and identification of invariantly associated proteins, implicitly supporting the PPI findings.

Both support cohesin analysis (C88-C90). OpenEval R30 notes strong statistical significance but mechanistic interpretation is somewhat speculative (association not causation), while peer R4 accepts the 3D chromatin interaction findings without raising concerns about causal claims.

Both support historical context (C124). OpenEval R31 notes appropriate citation to Ramaker and Partridge 2020 accurately reflecting field evolution, while peer R14 accepts the contextualization of the paradigm shift from artifacts to functional elements.
